chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Rifah ibn Musa, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man divorced his wife with one divorce, so she became fully divorced from him. Then another man married her and divorced her according to the Sunnah, so she became fully divorced from him. Then the first man married her again. How many divorces does she have with him? He said: She has no [remaining] divorces. Then he said: O Rifah, what if he divorced her three times, then married her a second time, and the divorce count was completed? If he then divorces her once, she has three [remaining] divorces.
ai.seo_question: How many divorces remain for a husband after his wife completes the triple divorce process with another man?
ai.summary: This narration from al-istibsar clarifies the Shia juristic distinction between a 'triple divorce' (talqatun thalath) that is immediately effective and one that is revocable, specifically addressing the scenario where a husband divorces his wife three times in a single sitting or session. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains that if the three divorces are treated as a single unit, the wife is not fully free (muharrarah) until she marries another man and he divorces her; however, if the divorces are counted individually, the status changes after the first or second, affecting the 'iddah and the requirement of a subsequent marriage (nizam). This highlights the Shia emphasis on the intention and manner of pronouncement in determining the finality of divorce, contrasting with some Sunni schools that view triple divorce as immediate and irrevocable.
